subject: Investigation: unusually high free-credit issuances — DataFlux cohort
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@dataflux.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, acctops@dataflux.ai
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerator credits for DataFlux pilot cohort

Hey team,

We've noticed multiple new users in our pilot receiving the 5000-token accelerator credit within minutes of sign-up. A few of the accounts look like variants of the same email (plus addressing and disposable domains) and several share device fingerprints that match prior test accounts. Can you pause any further self-serve credit grants to this tenant while we investigate? We attached a quick export of the suspect signups.

Olivia
Customer Success | DataFlux

Attachments: signup-logs-DF.csv (csv, 28KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: Investigate: DataFlux cohort — possible duplicate/automated signups (pausing grant)

Thanks Olivia — looping in infra and sales ops. I put an emergency hold on the self-serve accelerator grant rule for the DataFlux org (policy id: PLG-ACCEL-03) so new enrollments will not auto-credit while we triage.

Marcus — can you pull the issuance logs + device fingerprint matches and correlate with IP ranges? Aisha/Neha — what's the customer impact if we revoke recently granted credits (approx 14 accounts, ~70k tokens total)? We need a clear communication plan if we take action.

Action items:
- Marcus: issuance logs + cross-check device IDs (ETA 2 hours)
- Aisha: draft comms and advise on retention risk
- Neha: flag any active deals tied to these accounts in HS-4987

Thanks,
Soojin
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Investigate: DataFlux cohort — logs and matches attached

Attaching a quick findings summary — see device-fingerprints.json and trial-issuance-report.pdf. Early signals: 11 of the 14 accounts share a single device fingerprint and three more share an IP subnet that matches multiple signups over a 10-minute window. Two accounts used email aliases (plus addressing) on disposable domains. Timestamp correlation shows automated webhook calls from Onboardly between 09:08–09:12 which triggered our grant flow.

I recommend revoking the 11 clear duplicates and preserving the 3 borderline cases until we confirm (risk: false positive if a lot of users behind NAT).

Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer

Attachments: trial-issuance-report.pdf (PDF, 120KB); device-fingerprints.json (JSON, 48KB)

From: Onboardly Support <support@onboardly.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: webhook activity for DataFlux signups

Hi Marcus,

We pulled the webhook delivery logs you asked for. There was a brief burst of callbacks from DataFlux between 09:07:55 and 09:12:03 (PST) — payloads show 16 distinct signup events, 12 of which have identical device_fingerprint and similar user_agent strings. We also see three retries from the same originating IP (x.x.45.21).

If you need full payloads we can upload to your Drive share.

— Onboardly Support

Related link: https://drive.company/onboardly/dataflux/webhooks-20260301.json

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Investigate: DataFlux cohort — recommend revoke + comms

Thanks for the fast triage. Given the device fingerprint overlap and disposable domains, my recommendation is:

1) Revoke credits on the 11 accounts Marcus flagged (immediate, with internal note).
2) For the 3 ambiguous accounts, hold and reach out to the customer contact (Olivia) for context.
3) Offer DataFlux a one-time credit reissue for verified users (e.g., 2k tokens each) so they don't lose the pilot momentum.

Draft customer message (for review):
Hi Olivia — we detected anomalous signups that triggered auto-credits. To protect your pilot's integrity we've paused grants and revoked credits on accounts that look automated. We'll reissue credits for verified users and work with your team to tighten the onboarding hooks.

If we proceed, we should coordinate timing with support so there are no surprises in their dashboard.

Aisha
Account Executive

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@dataflux.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Final: action taken on suspicious accelerator credits + next steps

Olivia — thanks for your patience. Summary of actions taken on our side: 
- Placed hold on PLG-ACCEL-03 for DataFlux on 2026-03-01 09:30 PST.
- Revoked 11 accelerator grants where device_fingerprint == DFP_18934 and disposable-domain patterns were present (internal ticket: OPS-7241).
- Preserved 3 accounts pending manual verification — we'll coordinate with your CS team to confirm real users.
- Issued a one-time reconciled grant: 2k tokens to each verified user once confirmation is received.

We've attached the issuance report and device fingerprint export for your review. We will also add a short signature token check to the webhook payload as a quick mitigation to reduce automated replay.

Please let us know a good time for a 20-minute sync with your CS/Eng to walk through the evidence and the mitigation plan.

Thanks — looping legal if we need to run refunds or special billing.

Soojin Lee
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
